chunks: From him, from Ja'far, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The sale of dry dates for fresh dates is not valid, for fresh dates are moist and dry dates are dry; so when the fresh dates dry out, they lose weight."
ai.seo_question: Why is selling fresh dates for dry dates prohibited in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that exchanging dry dates (*tamr*) for fresh dates (*rutab*) is impermissible because the fresh dates will lose moisture and weight as they dry, introducing *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the final quantity. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on ensuring equivalence in commodities where natural degradation or transformation occurs post-transaction, preventing disputes over the actual value exchanged. It reflects the broader principle that sales involving perishable goods must account for the time lag between agreement and final delivery or drying.
